newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom shares could be unified in long term.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom shares could be unified in long term.

text.p: Shares in Russian natural gas group Gazprom, which has a two-tier system for foreign and domestic shares, could trade by one set of rules, but only after nine percent of the firm has been sold abroad, Prime-Tass news agency quoted an official as saying on Wednesday.

Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Brezgin told a press club rules for Gazprom shares could be unified only after nine percent of the company, the limit which Gazprom and the state have put on non-resident ownership, is sold abroad.
Gazprom has strongly defended the two-tier system of shares, by which American Depositary Shares (ADSs), each covering 10 local shares, are traded on Western markets at a three-fold premium.
One percent of Gazprom shares are so far covered by the ADSs, which see wide price swings when rumours of share unification are heeded by the market.
Gazprom closed on the Russian Trading System on Tuesday at $0.60, while the ADS closed in London at $18.80.
